description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Bellon Gambit. Meet 3...e4 with 4.Nd4! or break with 5.d3!.

drills.briefExplanation: 3.Nf3 e4 4.Nd4! — centralize the knight instead of retreating it.
drills.description: White to play. Black may push the Bellon 3...e4 — develop and know the knight maneuver.
drills.explanation: The refutation of the Bellon: after 3...e4, White doesn't retreat with 4.Ng5?? — instead 4.Nd4! centralizes the knight, attacking e6 and eyeing c6. Black's e4 wedge is now a target rather than a weapon: White will play d3 next, undermining it. Centralize against advanced pawns.
drills.name: The Nd4 Centralization

drills.briefExplanation: 3.Nf3 e4 4.Ng5 c6 5.d3! — lure the pawn forward, then undermine it.
drills.description: White to play. Black supported with 4...c6 — break the wedge with 5.d3!.
drills.explanation: If Black consolidates with 4...c6, White breaks with 5.d3! — challenging the e4 wedge at its base. After 5...exd3 6.Bxd3 White develops with tempo, the center opens for the bishops, and Black's 'space advantage' dissolves. Undermine advanced pawns; don't let them sit.
drills.name: The d3 Break

name: Bellon Gambit — White Tactics
